source: This is precisely the sort of rumor that could disintegrate all the hard work I've done. So I ask that you cease it.
A fascinating theory. Have you been standing in the summer sun too long?
Lady Brit is my wife's most faithful lady-in-waiting—and a young woman, too. She can do no harm to anyone.
Don't allow your whimsy to undermine affairs of state.
(Ugh. Looks like I'll have to find someone else to listen to me.)
Bernardo, you've got to believe me—Lady Brit is leaking information to Fortinbras's army.
Ophelia, this is a very serious accusation.
Extremely, incredibly serious.
I know. But you've known me my entire life. Have you ever known me to lie about something like this?
Won't you look into it as a favor?
Ah... you're correct in that regard, at least.
But Lady Birgitta is a respected member of the court—this must be pursued gently. I will speak with her, at the very least.
Yes, I've been informed of your suspicions. I will speak with her shortly.
Yes, I'm already aware. Unfortunately, it seems that it's too late for me to do anything.
If only I had known, perhaps circumstances would have taken a different turn.
Lady Brit is the one leaking information to Prince Fortinbras. I learned this firsthand.
Well, yes. We all did. Because Bernardo just announced it.
I find it such an unfortunate turn of events. That poor girl.
And why are you telling me about this? If that's the case, report it to the Guard Captain at once!
I thought you'd like to know.
Everyone knows, now!
But Ophelia, let me tell you something. She was a fool. Everyone knows there's a right way to commit treason.
I'd like to know when she's in jail for it!
But Ophelia, let me tell you something. If you've caught her, she's a fool. Everyone knows there's a right way to commit treason.
And that is?
Well, it's really very simple. I'm shocked more usurpers don't do this.
The first step is to ensure that any time you are committing treason, you're dressed exactly like your twin sister.
Then, when caught, you simply claim it was her. Off to the dungeon she goes, and you're free!
You... have a twin sister?
Well, of course. She lives at my parents' estate.
And you evidently don't like her very much.
Certainly not. She's dreadful.
How is one expected to acquire a twin sister in the first place?
Oh. Hmm. What an odd question! Ophelia, don't you know how children are made? You're old enough to know!
That's not what I was aski-- you know what, forget I said anything.
Irma, Lady Brit is a spy leaking information to Fortinbras.
Yes. We all heard the news!
She took advantage of my lady's trust. I cannot forgive her.
Still, to lose one's life so young-- it is a shame.
Many of us have done things worth regretting. Many of us are given a chance to redeem ourselves.
But there can be no redemption in execution.
Ophelia, please. I know Brit can be difficult, but this... this is too much.
You must come to love her as the Queen does. Do not try to overpower her. You are both strong, but not dissimilar...
Irma—you don't believe me?
Oh, Ophelia. You are so young. I forget sometimes how I was as a girl. Always with my teeth bared. Like you.
Laertes, I'm sorry to have to tell you this—but Brit is a spy working for Prince Fortinbras.
Brit? Working for... Norway?
You're serious? Truly?
Truly. I'm sorry. I really am. I know it may sound insane, but you of all people should speak with her. You'll learn the truth.
I want to believe you, but about Brit? I just...
I'll talk to her. I hope with all my soul you're wrong.
I know it seems strange, but please believe me. I think she means to have me killed.
And I don't know how to stop her without your help.
I'll tell the docksmen they can forget the boat, at least, for now. I shan't go to Paris. Not until this matter is resolved.
Won't Father be upset about the waste of time?
This is more important. Let me deal with Father separately.
I should have never trusted her.
It doesn't matter. None of it matters any longer.
I want her to pay for what she did. And yet...
Ergh. How can I travel with something like this weighing on me?
Lady Brit is a spy working for Prince Fortinbras.
Oh, my! You're drawing ever nearer, aren't you?
Not long now until she's paid for her crimes, I suspect.
Do keep this information moving towards the brawny arms of justice. I so love a good procedural drama.
That may be, but she's no longer a threat to you. Don't you remember?
I made some edits to the tale! Snip, snip... those bits are on the floor!
Are you going to imprison an innocent woman just to see what happens next?
If so, I must confess, I rather like your style.
Errrr, this is a matter for Cap'n Bernardo!
I dunno wot to do about spies... only loose chickens... an' rowdy servant boys.
Well, yeh! On account o' Bernardo announcin' it, we all know now!
It's always the ones yeh least expect, innit?
One time, someone stole my only good pair o' boots. Spent all day askin' around for 'em.
I interrogated a few o' the junior guards over it. Finally realized exactly who it was.
I'd gotten drunk an' lost them in the mud.
I was lookin' for the culprit... but the culprit was right under my nose all along!
I hear Quince will be performing soon. And Hamlet will be helping run the show.
So I've heard. The performance takes place soon, I believe, yes?
Is that so?
Maybe it's good the boy is applying himself to something.
Have you heard that Peter Quince is returning to put on a performance—with Hamlet assisting?
Heard? Why, love, I invited him myself.
It thrills me to see Hamlet getting involved. He needs something to perk his spirits.
The last time we had players at Elsinore, he was so much younger.
He fell asleep during the performance—his father had to carry him to bed.
I'm glad to see he's developed such an appreciation of the arts.
Have you heard that Peter Quince will perform? And Hamlet is assisting him.
So I've heard.
What is this sudden interest in art? That boy never had any head at all for art, and now suddenly the bird sings a new tune.
This old woman is suspicious and she doesn't like it.
Have you heard Peter Quince is going to perform? Hamlet's going to help with the show, too.
So I've heard. 6:00 PM, I believe, yes?
You know, Quince is an odd one. Always traipsing the countryside earning his coin from God-knows-what. It certainly isn't an honest living, at any rate.
And he's always smiling. What's so worth smiling about?
Are you looking forward to performing again in Elsinore?
I'm not here for them, my dear. I'm here for you.
But of course, I'm always up for a little fun.
Remember that if you'd like to see a special performance, you have only to request the topic du jour.
Remember you agreed to meet me in the gallery. It's long overdue.
Of all the places a man can perform, none are so impressive as a royal castle.
Of course, none are so hard to please as a royal court—why, mock the wrong face, and you're sure to lose a limb or three.
I come here as often as I can. Each time, I seem to find new inspiration.
I've seen your performances. They are... rather on point, aren't they?
I could almost swear they were about real people.
Oh ho ho! I do strive for believability, yes. I have my own patented technique!
I sense, however, that you may have some familiarity my work, already.
If you are interested in seeing me perform something special - maybe based upon some juicy gossip - feel free to let me know!
So! You're going to help put on a play, I hear.
What? Where... where did you hear that?
Oh—ah—not yet, of course.
But you know, I've heard that Peter Quince's one-man show may be coming by the castle soon.
Interesting. I'll keep a watchful eye.
Would that I had time for such an endeavor.
What a distant thing that seems like, now.
That's correct.
Any further thoughts?
You asked. I answered. What more do we have to discuss?
I dearly hope you can attend the performance. Tragedy can be so cathartic.
I've heard Quince will be performing soon—and Hamlet is assisting him.
Ho! It's been quite some time since I saw 'im last!
Yeh know, I saw 'im when King Hamlet was on the throne—God rest his soul—and King Alexander before him. This'll be the first time he's come to the present court.
Makes me feel old! Har har har...
So you've heard that Peter Quince is to perform soon?
Oh, have I! And the man's one of those types, too.
Those types?
Theater people. You know the sort. Always bursting into song for no reason. Always jittering around like they've been seized by the Holy Ghost.
Ugh. You stay away from them, Ophelia. Or before you know it, you'll be monologuing all over the place!
Ah! So like Hamlet, you mean?
...This has been a revelation. I need a moment.
Oh, yes. His Highness himself informed us. It's all a grand ceremony to lift Hamlet's mood.
I didn't realize Hamlet liked the theater so much these days.
Yes, well, you know, you're one of his old friends. He's been at Wittenberg with us for so long, you see.
One's tastes do tend to change when one runs in new social circles, you know.
Maybe I don't know him as well as I thought I did.
I had a strange nightmare where I saw the entire royal court killed.
And now you know it to be the truth.
It is the original fate of this world. And your death the crux of it all.
The Book of Fates, of course, saved you from death and chose you to be my unwilling partner in this game.
And yet you've opted not to make a move! So annoying.
I won't give you that satisfaction yet.
As I've said before, I'm a very patient man. I'll be here. Waiting.
An ill omen.
And what shall you do about it?
I'm not certain. But do you know whether I can stop it?
That depends on the genre of the performance!
In a comedy, of course. A comedy must always end happily.
But in a tragedy... well.
I wonder which one you're in?
I had a strange nightmare where I saw the royal court killed.
...Why are you wasting my time with this?
I have far more important things to worry about than your night terrors.
